decisions.executionNote: Approach basket with left arm while pitching gripper downward; board specifies the blue race car. Right arm stays clear.
Previous motion was rejected without execution; halve increments to establish a continuous elbow-up approach.
Advance left gripper toward moving basket handle with continuous downward pitch; estimate handle depth from head view.
Reduce combined rotation and translation after IK rejection; continue basket interception.
Position left gripper over the basket's left handle region as it travels right, finishing downward orientation without crossing center.
Use the reachable left rim instead of a large wrist rotation; align open fingers around the moving rim at current height.
Align around left basket rim, close, and begin a short test lift; retention must be checked visually.
Basket was not retained and has entered right workspace. Withdraw left arm and approach its right side with right arm, leaving left available for the trailing blue car.
Advance right fingers to the basket's right rim while prepositioning the open left gripper toward the blue car, without picking before basket lift.
Set right fingers slightly lower around the right rim, close while following conveyor, and test lift. Keep left open over the approaching car.
Raise the closed right gripper 12 cm to verify basket retention and required lift. Lower open left fingers toward the blue car without yet grasping.
Basket visibly follows the raised right hand. Follow and pinch the blue car with left fingers, then test lift; shift suspended basket inward while right arm remains on its side.
Left wrist shows fingers short of the car body; reopen and reach slightly farther forward and lower before closing again. Keep basket elevated near the shared center.
Test retention by lifting the pinched blue car vertically with a small inward shift. Maintain the visibly suspended basket and both closed grippers.
Car remained on belt. Reopen and change to a more vertical approach over the cockpit while tracking it; keep basket suspended.
Fingers remain visibly above the car. Descend and turn the vertical gripper to pinch across the car's narrow body while following the conveyor.
Replan from the single executed step with smaller yaw increments. Continue lowering open fingers toward the blue car.
Open jaws now flank the blue cockpit at belt height. Close while tracking, then lift to check retention; stop descending against the observed contact.
Previous pinch missed to the near-left of the cockpit. Reopen, correct rightward and forward with the moving car, lower around its body, and close again.
Lift closed left fingers vertically with slight clearance from the basket; inspect whether the car follows rather than relying on gripper state.
Replan after lift IK interruption. Visible fingertips are offset left of the car; correct that offset and lower for a new pinch, shifting suspended basket right for clearance.
Lift and slightly retract the newly closed car grasp to avoid the folded-elbow limit. Hold basket steady and inspect whether the car leaves the belt.
Wrist view shows the car offset forward from the closed fingertips. Reopen and correct forward and slightly inward before one more pinch, keeping left EE on its side.
Test the nose-area pinch by lifting and retracting left, watching for car motion relative to the belt; maintain right basket hold.
Car has entered right workspace. Prepare a basket handoff: bring basket centrally with right, reorient open left fingers toward its left rim, keeping arm separation.
Finish matching the successful rim-grasp orientation and bring left jaws around the basket's left side; keep right closed until left retention can be tested.
Close left around the opposite rim, then release and withdraw right slowly to test the basket handoff while preserving elevation.
Basket shifted during handoff; resecure with right while seating left fingers slightly inward and lower around the left rim.
Separate the arms gently to verify whether left retains the basket; right opens and withdraws toward the car workspace.
Left did not retain the basket. Reclose right at the visible rim and bring it inward again before attempting a more precise left-side grasp.
Basket no longer follows the right hand. Reopen and approach its outer rim lower, rather than pinching empty interior; left remains clear.
Seat right fingers across the outer rim, close while following its motion, then make a visible lift test before transporting.
Wrist image indicates the closed fingers were inside rather than across the wall. Reopen, shift outward to the wall and lower before closing and testing lift.
Allow a full open interval and descend to the lower rim-grasp height that previously retained the basket, tracking its conveyor motion.
Close fully around the visible rim while matching belt motion, allowing settling before a short lift test.
Basket visibly rotated with the closed rim grasp. Lift it clear by 11 cm and transport inward for a left-hand support transfer.
Basket is now visibly retained and elevated. Bring its left wall between the left fingers, seating those fingers below the rim for a secure transfer.
Close left at the lower wall contact and let it settle before right releases; use a small left lift to verify support transfer.
Test left basket support while sending the open right gripper toward the blue car approaching the right edge; retain arm separation.
Basket was not retained by left. Intercept the blue car with right before it leaves reach; approach open at body height, keeping left clear.
After the continuity stop, use small increments toward the wrist-visible car cockpit and lower the open fingers before closing.
Retract inward and lift the closed right grasp away from the reach boundary. Basket occludes the car, so retention remains uncertain until the lift is visible.
The car was not retained. Turn the right gripper toward the outward conveyor direction so the fingers can reach it without further extending the arm; lift clear of the tipped basket.
Continue the outward-facing approach, lowering toward the car and aligning jaws across its width; use wrist reach rather than crossing or changing elbow configuration.
Car is now between the outward-facing jaws in the wrist view but below them. Descend cautiously with a small alignment correction; basket contact may limit progress.
Significant residual suggests basket obstruction rather than a car grasp. Lift and retract the closed fingers to clear contact and determine what, if anything, is retained.
The retraction was rejected without movement. Reduce increments substantially and lift away from obstructing contact while retaining the current configuration.
Retract the possible basket-wall grasp into the reachable region and lift clear, then verify retention visually before another placement attempt.
Basket now visibly follows right. Bring it centrally while rotating back toward a forward-facing, reachable hold; car remains outside the basket.
Bring the retained basket into the central handoff region and lower open left fingers toward its near-left wall; do not release right support yet.
Left inner fingertip is still outside the basket wall. Move the open jaw pair inward and lower around that wall while right holds it stationary.
Left fingers now visibly contact the basket wall. Close and settle, then cautiously release right support and test a small left-hand lift.
Left support remains unverified. Reclose right and bring the basket farther left within arm separation, withdrawing the open left hand to avoid collision.
Seat left fingers farther forward and below the visible left rim, then close while keeping right support. Car is currently out of the head view.
Allow the seated left grasp to settle, then release and separate right while gently lifting left to verify whether the basket follows.
The left wrist still shows the wall beyond the fingertips. Reopen and insert farther forward and inward at a lower height while right resecures support.
Bring the supported left rim into the open left jaw pair with small relative motions, then close without removing right support.
Verify the seated left grasp by lifting and shifting it left while the open right hand withdraws completely from the basket.
Basket followed right rather than left. Reclose right and shift it farther into left reach, raising the open left hand for clearance while preserving separate arm workspaces.
Basket is finally centered with its left wall well inside left reach. Descend the open left fingers around that wall while right holds position.
No motion executed after the continuity rejection. Halve the descent and lateral increments from the observed pose, maintaining the existing elbow-up configuration.
Continue the smaller descent to seat the open left jaws around the basket's left wall, keeping the right-hand support fixed.
Correct the remaining lateral gap to the basket's left rim with the open left gripper, then close while keeping the right support unchanged.
Let the left rim pinch settle, then withdraw the open right hand and lift left to verify basket retention from the resulting image.
Prior left pinches were above the lower basket wall. Reopen and descend to the wall rather than handle height, with right maintaining support.
Change left to a more vertical rim approach to clear the handle obstruction, keeping the fingers open and right support fixed.
Replan from the seven executed steps with smaller rotation increments; align the more vertical left fingers around the wall without removing right support.
Vertical fingertips are still visibly above the left rim. Lower the open gripper to the wall, make a small inward correction, then close with right support maintained.
Stop descending against contact and allow the left pinch to settle. Release right cautiously and make only a small left lift to check retention.
Left retention remains unconfirmed. Clear the left hand, resecure right, and gently turn the supported basket to expose an accessible rim rather than repeating the obstructed approach.
Align the vertical left fingers with the newly exposed left corner, keeping the left EE on its side and the right basket support stationary.
Close and settle the left fingers around the now-visible wall within the jaw opening, then cautiously release right without a large motion.
Test left retention with a small lift and retreat while moving the fully open right hand clear. Basket motion, not commanded closure, will determine whether the transfer held.
The basket again followed right, not left. Reclose right and relocate it farther into the left workspace while keeping the open left hand clear and both EEs on their own sides.
Align the vertical left jaw pair with the exposed left corner using a small inward descent; hold the right-supported basket stationary.
The wall now spans the left jaw opening in the wrist view. Close and settle before a minimal right release, then verify support visually.
Test the left wall grasp by lifting and retracting left while moving the fully open right hand clear; judge retention from basket motion.
